cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')

exact_cwe_mechanism.evidence: Direct shell command execution via child_process.exec() with string interpolation of externally-influenced SHA value matches CWE-78 definition

connection.evidence: tag parameter flows through git rev-parse to sha variable, then directly interpolated into shell command; demonstrated path: tag → git rev-parse → sha → git checkout command

diff_causality.evidence: This line is the vulnerable command execution itself; reverting would remove the injection point entirely

security_control.evidence: sha.trim() removes whitespace but provides no protection against command injection; exec() used instead of safer spawn() with separate arguments
security_control.required_control: Proper command parameterization or input validation for shell command arguments
security_control.control_requirement_evidence: CWE-78 requires neutralization of special shell characters when constructing OS commands from external input
existing_controls_checked: git rev-parse execution with tag parameter
security_control.deficiency_evidence: No validation of SHA format or neutralization of shell metacharacters; direct string interpolation into shell command

concrete_impact.evidence: Arbitrary command execution possible if attacker controls tag parameter to inject shell commands through SHA manipulation

diff_counterfactual: If the candidate line were reverted, the git checkout command execution with interpolated SHA would not occur, eliminating the command injection vulnerability.
supporting_evidence: run() function uses child_process.exec() for shell command execution
SHA value from git rev-parse ${tag} directly interpolated into shell command string
No parameterization or validation of SHA format before command execution
unresolved_facts: Exact validation and constraints on tag parameter values before reaching this function
Whether git rev-parse provides any inherent protection against command injection through tag parameter
review_comment: The git checkout command executes with SHA value directly interpolated into the shell command string, creating a command injection vulnerability. The sha.trim() only removes whitespace but does not prevent shell metacharacter injection. Replace the string interpolation with spawn() using separate arguments: use child_process.spawn('git', ['checkout', sha.trim()], {cwd: repoDir}) to safely execute the command without shell interpretation.
